summary.text: A declarative control plane schedules and supervises arbitrary agent commands in isolated task environments.

maturity.text: v0.3.0 follows a major September 2026 rewrite. Its v1alpha1 API and core concepts remain unstable.

advantages.text: The control-plane/runner boundary can accommodate different harnesses and languages.
Declarative resources make workspace, egress and workload lifecycle visible to an operator.

tradeoffs.text: Requires Kubernetes, Redis, Agent Substrate and container infrastructure.
MCP and skill registries are declared in the schema, but the current default workspace setup does not materialize them.

taskFit.text: Infrastructure teams operating many isolated agent workloads or evaluation tasks.
Workloads that need durable workspaces, suspend/resume and operator inspection.

nodes.label: Task manifests
nodes.subtitle: Task · Workspace · Gateway · Model

responsibility.text: Declares workload configuration as typed resources in the ax.io/v1alpha1 API.

nodes.extension: Images, commands, repositories and policies are configurable.
nodes.failureMode: A declared field is not proof that the default runner implements its behavior.

nodes.label: ax-server
nodes.subtitle: Stateless gRPC API

responsibility.text: Validates and stores resources, publishing task events for controllers.

nodes.extension: The API is independent of the agent process.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.subtitle: Resource hashes + event stream

responsibility.text: Stores resource state and distributes reconciliation work through Redis Streams.

nodes.outputs: Controller work and watchable task status
nodes.extension: Controllers consume through a consumer group.
nodes.failureMode: Queue state and the sandbox's own persistent state are different stores.

nodes.label: ax-controller
nodes.subtitle: Reconcile desired state

responsibility.text: Ensures an Agent Substrate atespace, template and actor exist, then applies lifecycle and egress decisions.

nodes.outputs: Actor creation, policy and suspend/resume requests
nodes.extension: Controllers can run as multiple consumers.
nodes.failureMode: Reconciliation is a distributed workflow, not a model sampling loop.

nodes.label: Gateway policy
nodes.subtitle: Outbound hosts and ports

responsibility.text: Describes listeners and outbound network access applied to the task environment.

nodes.extension: Host and port allowlists are declarative.
nodes.failureMode: The default without a restrictive gateway allows port 443 to all hosts.

nodes.label: Agent Substrate
nodes.subtitle: Actor isolation + snapshots

responsibility.text: Supplies the execution environment and durable snapshots used for task suspension and resumption.

nodes.extension: AX delegates isolation and actor lifecycle to this substrate.
nodes.failureMode: Suspend/resume preserves workspace state; it is not a conversation abstraction.

nodes.label: ax-task-runner
nodes.subtitle: PID 1 and workspace setup

responsibility.text: Prepares repositories, starts guest services and supervises the configured command inside the task.

nodes.outputs: A running child process and guest services
nodes.extension: Extend or replace the runner using its documented contract.
nodes.failureMode: The current runner does not automatically turn every child exit into a completed control-plane task.

nodes.label: Agent command
nodes.subtitle: Your chosen harness

responsibility.text: Runs the actual agent inside the task. That process owns any model–tool loop and conversation logic.

nodes.extension: Any compatible image/command can supply the workload.
nodes.failureMode: A hosted harness must still configure its own credentials and tool policies.

chapters.title: Declare the workload
chapters.heading: A different architectural layer
chapters.body: AX runs the environment around an agent. Begin with its four declarative resources.
chapters.takeaway: The agent's model–tool loop belongs to the hosted command.

chapters.title: The control plane
chapters.heading: Desired state becomes a task
chapters.body: Follow resource updates through Redis and the controller's reconciliation loop.
chapters.takeaway: Reconciliation coordinates infrastructure, not assistant reasoning.

chapters.title: Isolation and networking
chapters.heading: Draw the execution boundary
chapters.body: Agent Substrate supplies actors and snapshots; Gateway specifies network policy.
chapters.takeaway: Network policy, resource limits and human approval are different controls.

chapters.title: The runner contract
chapters.heading: Inside the task
chapters.body: The runner prepares a workspace and launches the selected command.
chapters.takeaway: A custom runner is AX's main extension seam.

chapters.title: Before and after v0.3
chapters.heading: Read history in context
chapters.body: The September rewrite removed the previous built-in harness. Current MCP and skill declarations also differ from default setup behavior.
chapters.takeaway: Do not combine historical and current capabilities into one architecture.
